name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+17
Incumbent Gary Palmer is running with a large fundraising advantage
Democratic challenger has raised almost nothing ($6,539) with no outside support
Prediction markets price the Democrat at roughly 4 percent
model.rationale: This is a deeply Republican Birmingham-suburban district where incumbent Gary Palmer is seeking another term, and the Democratic challenger has raised only a few thousand dollars with no outside spending against Palmer. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Republican hold, so the forecast stays close to the district's partisan lean.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unexpectedly strong Democratic fundraising surge would be the only realistic path to moving this race toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gary Palmer is the incumbent in Alabama's 6th District, a Birmingham-area seat that leans about 17 points Republican. He is running for reelection and has raised more than $1 million, holding over $260,000 in cash, with outside groups spending in his support and none against him.

Democratic nominee Maurice Mercer has raised under $7,000 and reports less than $2,000 on hand, with no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 4 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong partisan lean, Palmer's incumbency, and the lopsided resource gap makes this a safe Republican seat, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the winning margin.
